newsitem.title: USA: RailAmerica buys stake in Chilean rail.
newsitem.headline: RailAmerica buys stake in Chilean rail.

text.p: RailAmerica Inc said on Friday that its Chilean unit has acquired a majority interest in the stock of Empressa de Transporte Ferroviario SA, a 1,400 mile railroad serving northern Chile.

RailAmerica has joined in the purchase of Ferronor with Andres Pirazzoli Y Cia Ltda, a family-owned Chilean transportation and distribution company, from a Chilean government agency, the company said.

The purchase price paid by RailAmerica/APCO for substantially all of the stock of Ferronor was approximately $12 million and was funded 55 percent by RailAmerica and 45 percent by Andrex Pirazzoli, the company said.
The sale of Ferronor by Corporacion de Fomento de la Produccion, an agency of the Chilean government, is a continuation of Chile's privatization process, RailAmerica said.
RailAmerica said Ferronor operates the only north-south railroad in northern Chile, extending from La Calera near Santiago.

Ferronor also operates several east-west branch lines that link a number of iron, copper and limestone mines and production processing facilities with several Chilean Pacific port cities, RailAmerica said.
Ferronor also serves Argentina and Bolivia through traffic interchanged with the General Belgrano Railroad and the Ferrocarriles Antofagasta Bolivia.
Ferronor, which employs 350 people, currently operates 32 locomotives and some 700 rail cars and hauls more than 60,000 carloads per year, RailAmerica said.

RailAmerica said it expects Ferronor's traffic to increase significantly from a long-term contract tor haul up to six million tons of iron pellets a year starting in 1998, increased copper shipping, and increased international volume with its Latin American neighbors through the Mercosor trade agreement.
